title: His daughter's ambitions and singing
summary: Edison encourages education over a singing career for his daughter, who likes rock but is coming to love Ella.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: What do you think she'd like to do?
She wants to be a doctor, to be a plastic surgeon.
Well, you know how kids are. They say they want to be -- no telling what she'll --
But she's got that in her mind.
She's got that in her mind now. She's a good singer, she's a very good singer. But I try to discourage that right now, you know.
I know too much. Yeah, I try to discourage that and I try to encourage education.
Because there are so many people like in the sports world and entertainment world that have made money

and their managers end up with all the money, the promoter or the -- they cut you up so many ways, you know. And I tell her that, "You're gifted with a gift that nobody can take from you, which is singing, but you're not gifted with an education. You have to learn that, you have to acquire that, and it takes years of concentration and diligence and devotion to acquire an education. And then, if you decide to sing, that can be a hobby. Singing can be a hobby, you know." And I try to encourage education. I stress that first.
Well, in what way does she sing? What sort of songs?
She sings her own little style, you know. She goes for the rock and roll, you know. But she's beginning to like -- she loves Ella.

She loves Ella, yeah. And I'm so glad, because the records that she used to play, I couldn't even understand the words, you know. But she could. It's funny about this generation. They can understand what they sing and I can't, you know.
